title: Normalized presentations of abelian inverse image
statement: Let $(C,J)$ and $(D,K)$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $L:\operatorname{Sh}(J,\mathrm{Set})\to\operatorname{Sh}(K,\mathrm{Set})$ be a functor. An abelian inverse-image presentation of $L$ consists of a functor $A:\operatorname{Ab}(J)\to\operatorname{Ab}(K)$ and a natural isomorphism $e:|A(-)|\cong L(|-|)$, with the following graph normalizations. For every abelian sheaf $M$, test sheaf $T$, and arrows $a,b,t:T\to |M|$ satisfying $t=a+b$ on every section, the arrows $e_M^{-1}L(a),e_M^{-1}L(b),e_M^{-1}L(t)$ satisfy the same equation on every section of $L(T)$. Likewise a sectionwise zero arrow remains zero. Naturality of $e$ specifies the underlying action on morphisms. When $L$ preserves finite limits these conditions express precisely transport of addition and zero along its finite-product and terminal-object comparisons; additive inverses are determined by addition and zero. No adjunction or exactness on abelian sheaves is part of the datum.
